Claude Buddy can now start a chat as well as watch one, and when it opens a terminal in iTerm2, Claude Code is actually running in it. Those two are this release.

0.5.5-beta was a single crash fix. This one clears everything that has landed since: two features, four fixes you would have noticed, and two that make the test suite trustworthy.

Still a beta. What was and was not verified on a real machine is in *Known limitations*.

## New: start a chat from Claude Buddy

Until now Claude Buddy only ever *observed* sessions. **New chat…** in the tray menu opens a small dialog: pick Claude Code, Codex, Grok or OpenClaw, pick a folder (recent session folders first, then Browse…), and press Start. **New chat here** on an orb's context menu opens the same dialog already filled in with that orb's folder and CLI.

For OpenClaw the folder field becomes an agent picker, and Start creates a conversation on the gateway and opens a chat panel on it.

A kind that can't be used is shown disabled, with the reason on screen: the CLI wasn't found, no gateway is configured, or replying to agents is turned off in Settings. A launch never fails silently. If no orb shows up within about twenty seconds of a successful start, the dialog says so.

## New: a sound when a turn finishes or a session needs you

A new **Sounds** section in Settings plays a sound when a turn finishes and a different one when a session is waiting on you. It has a preview for each. The choices are your system's own sounds or a file you pick, so nothing is bundled. Each orb can override the default from its right-click menu, under **Sound**.

Turn finished can instead speak a short summary of what was done, in the orb's own voice. Sounds from one scan are merged into one, attention wins over finished, and there is always at least two seconds between sounds. So a burst of agents finishing at once gives you one chime, not a chord.

## Fixed: iTerm2 opened a blank window instead of Claude Code

If iTerm2 is your terminal, every "open a terminal" path handed iTerm2 a shell command line it doesn't run through a shell. That covers opening an agent team's view, attaching to a teammate, and the new New chat dialog. iTerm2 tried to execute a program called `cd`. Depending on the moment, you got either a blank window and "Couldn't open a terminal for Claude Code", or, worse, a plain shell in your home directory while the app reported success. This dates from 0.5.4-beta.

iTerm2 now starts your own login shell (`$SHELL`, falling back to `/bin/zsh` for anything that can't parse the line) as a login, interactive shell. Your `.zshrc` PATH applies, so a `claude` under `~/.local/bin` or a node under nvm is found. The line goes to iTerm2 base64-encoded, because iTerm2's own argument splitter interprets backslashes even inside single quotes, and a folder name may legally contain one. Folders with spaces, apostrophes, quotes, `$` or `~` in their names now open exactly where they should.

The same change fixes a quieter bug on **both** iTerm2 and Terminal.app. With zoxide set up as your `cd`, a folder that no longer existed could fuzzy-match a similarly named project and start Claude there. It now fails the `cd` and runs nothing.

## Fixed: OpenClaw orbs never glowed while replying

An OpenClaw conversation replying to you left its orb dark. Only cron jobs lit up, because the original rule had been built from a cron job's events, and an ordinary run reports itself differently. The orb now glows for any run in flight, on a rule that counts an event as work only when its shape was measured to mean work, rather than on a blocklist of events that don't.

## Fixed: cloud sessions vanished after "Keep orbs for"

A cloud session you hadn't typed into recently lost its orb once the "Keep orbs for" window passed, even though it still exists and can be resumed at any time. That setting is about local sessions, where a quiet status file usually means a process that exited without saying so. A cloud session has no process to exit, so it now keeps its orb until you archive it.

## Fixed: a persona lost its picture one folder down

A persona set up with profile-gen kept its name and lost its picture, drawing letters instead, whenever the session sat in a subfolder of the project rather than the project folder itself. profile-gen writes the picture's path relative to the project folder. Claude Buddy only looked for it next to the persona file, which doubles the path, and under the session's current folder, which is only the project folder while you stay in it. One folder down, both missed.

Claude Buddy now remembers which folder level of its upward search found the persona, and looks for the picture there too, after the persona file's own folder and before the current folder. Verified on a real Mac: an orb in `~/Documents` now shows the same portrait as one in `~`, where it used to show the persona's initials.

Two deliberate widenings come with it. If the same picture name exists under both the project folder and your current folder, the project folder's copy now wins; before, the current folder's did. And a persona found from your home folder may use any picture under your home folder, because containment is checked per root and that root is `~`.

## Fixed: the test suite told the truth about itself, again

Two changes with no user-visible effect. The UI suite sometimes reported one test fewer than it has, with no failure and a clean exit. The cause was the test framework resetting the UI dispatcher before every test, which let a leftover background thread claim it. It now runs under one dispatcher: 30 runs before the change showed two short counts, and 30 after showed none. A flaky OpenClaw handshake test was also made deterministic.

## Known limitations

The iTerm2 fix was verified on a real iTerm2 3.7.3. That covers New chat and the agent-team launches, every command shape, 14 hostile folder names and bash, sh, dash and ksh as `$SHELL`. It was not verified by clicking Start in the installed app, on the path that places a new chat in an existing tmux session, or against real bash or ksh users' dotfiles. If a folder is deleted in the instant between New chat checking it and the terminal starting, iTerm2 briefly opens a window that closes, with no error in the dialog. A returned window proves a window opened, not that the command in it ran. If you use oh-my-zsh's `dotenv` plugin, it may ask "Source it?" in the new window, as it always has in Terminal.app.

Claude Code itself refuses a working directory containing a backslash, even when started by hand. That is upstream.

Windows is unaffected by the iTerm2 fix, which is macOS-only by construction. Both platforms run the full suite in CI.

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.6-beta-osx-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.6-beta-osx-x64.dmg` |
| Windows 10/11, 64-bit | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.6-beta-win-x64-setup.exe` |

## Upgrading

Replace the app as usual. On macOS, replacing `/Applications/Claude Buddy.app` gives the bundle a new code identity, and macOS re-evaluates the Automation and Local Network permissions against it. If click-to-focus or anything on your LAN stops working after an upgrade, look there first.
